summary: Guidance request: separate quotas for short-lived realtime sessions and long-lived batch uploads to avoid tenant 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer SpectraSearch runs a mixed workload on a dedicated pool: many short-lived websocket inference sessions (interactive agents) plus periodic large embedding/batch uploads. Over the past week their short-lived sessions have been getting 429s at the same time bulk backfills run. Customer suspects batch traffic is exhausting a shared tenant token bucket and wants guidance on separating quotas or tuning burst windows to avoid impacting real-time sessions.

Impact:
- Intermittent 429s on realtime websocket starts, causing poor UX for agents and reconnect storms.
- Bulk embedding jobs complete but cause retries and extra cost for the customer.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-west serving rw-infer-3.2 for streaming + embed-small-v1 for embeddings.
- SpectraSearch uses 40 concurrent websocket clients (short-lived, ~30s each) and scheduled batch uploader with 50 parallel workers for backfill windows.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start 40 websocket connections with a 5–10s stagger, have each send a short prompt to start generation and then disconnect after receiving stream finish.
2) Trigger the batch embedding job (50 parallel workers) for a ~1M-record backfill.
3) Observe websocket connection starts receive 429s until the batch slims down.

Expected behavior:
- Dedicated pool should isolate short interactive sessions from heavy batch writes or allow configurable burst isolation so small sessions are not penalized.

Actual behavior:
- Websocket start attempts get 429s during peak batch activity. Throttling recovers once batch workers slow down or finish.

Logs / artifacts attached by customer:
- Packet capture of websocket handshake failures (attached in ticket).
- Console screenshot showing per-route latency spike and a token-bucket saturation alert at 2026-03-06T03:42:00Z.
- Link to their job run: https://jobs.spectrasearch.com/runs/0982-backfill
comments: 2026-03-08 09:15 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Assigned to Maya for initial triage. Asked customer for exact backoff/retry behavior and if they use ephemeral API keys for workers.

2026-03-08 11:02 - SpectraSearch (customer): We use a single service key for both websocket clients and batch workers. Websockets are short-lived (open -> single prompt -> close). Batch workers are long-lived processes. We can separate keys if needed but prefer platform guidance.

2026-03-09 14:30 - Maya Chen (Support): Reproduced locally with a similar mix against a staging dedicated pool. Observed tenant token bucket exhaustion when parallel batch workers exceed 30 concurrent heavy token-rate clients. Websocket starts consume requests that count against the same tenant window. Suggestion: separate quotas by route or by API key to guarantee small interactive window.

2026-03-10 08:12 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Added investigation note — rate-limiter code uses a single tenant_token_bucket with a short-window burst of 1s and long-window refill. We can use per-route weighting now (config) or create a second bucket scoped to route="realtime". Tested quick patch to prefer route-affinity during accounting; reduced websocket 429s in staging.

2026-03-12 16:01 - SpectraSearch (customer): We tested assigning a separate API key for websocket clients and saw immediate improvement. Can you provide recommended production config we should request of our Redwood Dedicated admin?
2026-03-13 09:42 - Maya Chen (Support): Provided recommended config and follow-ups below.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Shared tenant-level token bucket is being consumed by long-lived batch workers which generate many tokens per second, leaving insufficient tokens for short websocket start requests that are bursty.

Staging repro: Simulated 40 short websocket clients + 50 batch workers; token-bucket depleted within ~30s of batch start. Websocket START endpoint is charged heavier due to per-request overhead (auth + route lookup) and counts against tenant window.

Observability: Token bucket metrics (tenant.tokens_available) showed sawtooth pattern; refill rate matched committed quota but instantaneous consumption exceeded burst budget. Per-route metrics available in console but not enforced in our customers' config by default.

Temporary mitigation tested: Assigning separate API key to websocket clients leads to separate per-key buckets and immediate reduction in 429s. Implemented per-route soft-weights in staging rate-limiter and saw websocket 429s drop by 90% under identical load.

Risk notes: Creating strict per-route isolation reduces batch throughput slightly during backfills because batch workers lose access to aggregated burst tokens; recommend a readjusted committed rate or scheduled backfill windows.
Related code pointers: rate-limiter/token_bucket.go and route-weighting feature flag. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/842 for prototype weight-based accounting.
Next steps: Provide customer with documented config options, example API key separation steps, and a recommended rate-limiter config for Dedicated tenants.
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround (confirmed effective): Create two service API keys: one used exclusively by websocket/interactive clients (low-volume, high-priority) and one used by batch workers. This isolates per-key token buckets and eliminated websocket 429s in customer's tests.

Recommended Dedicated config changes (production):
- Enable per-route token-bucket isolation, with route tag 'realtime' weight=1 and 'batch' weight=0.6.
- Configure a dedicated small-burst reserve for 'realtime' with a short burst window (2s) and a higher refill priority.
- If using a single key, set per-route min_quota for 'realtime' to guarantee N start requests/sec during backfills.
- Consider scheduling large backfills to windows with lower interactive load or throttling batch worker concurrency to a safe ceiling (e.g., 30 workers).

Operational recommendations for SpectraSearch:
1) Create two keys, rotate batch worker key before starting backfills.
2) Add jittered stagger on websocket connect (already doing 5–10s) — keep it.
3) Ask Redwood Dedicated admin to apply route-weighting config sample attached.
4) If cost is acceptable, increase committed capacity for the dedicated pool during large backfills to preserve interactive SLAs.

Follow-up items created:
- INT-21392: Add a console UI knob to recommend per-route quota suggestions for mixed workloads (owner: product infra).
- SUP-517215: Post-deploy verification with SpectraSearch after they apply config (owner: Maya).

Customer confirmed: After applying separate keys and applying recommended route weights in a staging Dedicated config, websocket 429s stopped producing errors. Customer will schedule production change 2026-03-20 and requested rollback plan in case of regressions.
